REGULAR MEETING AGENDA - REVISED
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 25, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 819 3070 2970
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS AND THE PUBLIC MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public subject to Los Angeles County mandated COVID-19 protocols. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will also be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below, or in-person subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using any of the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81930702970
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 819 3070 2970
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
MARCH 25, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN HYBRID MODE FROM THE COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA AND VIA TELECONFERENCE AS AUTHORIZED BY
STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20, VIA ZOOM VIDEO
COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID# 819 3070 2970

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Naresh Solanki.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  March as Women’s History Month (recognizing the efforts of the Woman’s Club of Artesia-
  Cerritos).

  Mayor Solanki read from a letter submitted by a Cerritos resident who commended Mayor Pro
  Tem Vo’s efforts in providing voluntary safety training to the community.

5A.  Closed Session report from the Thursday, March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting

  Pam Lee, Interim City Attorney, provided the following report:

  The City Council met in Closed Session to discuss Item 12A as listed on the Thursday,
  March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Agenda:

  12A.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED LITIGATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) (COUNCIL)
  Number of cases: One (1)

  With regard to Item 12A, the City Council discussed the matter and no reportable action
  was taken. This concluded the Closed Session report.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 7

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Mel Cortez thanked the City Council for the COVID-19 Memorial Illumination and the
  Sheriff’s Department for the catalytic converter anti-theft training. He inquired regarding
  the stolen public art statue on Artesia Boulevard and whether it would be replaced.

  Daisy Legasca thanked the City Council for recognizing the Woman’s Club of Artesia-Cerritos
  and expressed opposition to hate crimes against Asian American/Pacific Islanders.

  Tom Tislow expressed appreciation for those veterans who served in the Vietnam War.

  Sam Desai encouraged the City Council to consider and enact policies which support local
  small businesses.

  Noting there no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to speak,
  the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the Tuesday, March 9, 2021, 2:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special
  Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to approve the Tuesday, March 9, 2021,
  2:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Approval of the Thursday, March 11, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency
  Regular Meeting Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to approve the Thursday, March 11,
  2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 25, 2021
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to approve the Register of Demands as
  follows:

  City of Cerritos  March 25, 2021  $ 6,067,074.95 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of an informational update on the City's response to the COVID-
  19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to receive and file the informational
  report on the City's response to the COVID-19 local emergency (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of a request for City consent to the assignment of a sublease for
  the Land Rover/Jaguar dealership located at 10861 183 rd Street, Cerritos, California,
  90703, from LRJ Automotive LLC, a subsidiary of SoCal Penske Dealer Group, to Envision
  CE LRJ Auto LLC, and approval and authorization for the City in its capacity as ground
  lessor/landlord to execute an estoppel certificate, ground lease amendment, and a
  sublease recognition, non-disturbance and attornment agreement associated with the
  assignment of the sublease (APN 7034-017-909) (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were presented by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager, and Dennis Roy,
  Assistant City Attorney. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 4 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  provided written correspondence or elected to speak, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to authorize the Mayor, or his
  designee, to execute the documents to facilitate, acknowledge and consent to the transfer
  of the sublease for the City-owned property located at 10861 183rd Street, from LRJ
  Automotive LLC, a subsidiary of SoCal Penske Dealer Group, to Envision CE LRJ Auto LLC,
  or another affiliated entity of Envision Motors, which has been approved by the City, in
  such form as the City Attorney shall deem appropriate, including any estoppel certificates,
  ground lease amendments, or related documentation required or appropriate in connection
  with completion of such assignment in the forms attached hereto or such other form as the
  City Attorney shall deem appropriate (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of a request to sell the five-acre City-owned parcel located east
  of the San Gabriel River channel, west of Dumont Avenue, between 183rd Street and
  Artesia Boulevard (APN 7034-018-901) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherrè Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent, and Pam Lee,
  Interim City Attorney. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Mel Cortez spoke in opposition to the sale of the subject property to the current lessee, B &
  B Stables, and inquired regarding potential conflicts of interest of City Council members as
  related to voting on this item.

  Mary Buell, representing B & B Stables, spoke in support of their proposal to purchase the
  subject property, noting their long-standing community therapeutic riding program.

  Sam Desai spoke in opposition to the sale of the subject property to the current lessee, B &
  B Stables, and inquired regarding potential conflicts of interest of City Council members as
  related to voting on this item.

  Murali Vasudevan spoke in opposition to the sale of the subject property to the current
  lessee, B & B Stables, and inquired regarding potential conflicts of interest of City Council
  members as related to voting on this item.

  Daisy Legasca inquired as to the ethical considerations related to this item.

  Noting there were no others individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to direct the City Manager to analyze
  the feasibility of amending the current lease terms with B & B Stables as related to the
  subject property for a longer term lease, similar to the terms B & B Stables has in place
  with Southern California Edison (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of a monumental scale Chihuly studio art piece to be located in
  the Cerritos Library located at 18025 Bloomfield Avenue (APN 7025-028-907) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Sorin (last name not provided) submitted written correspondence in opposition of the art
  piece, and suggested community involvement in the selection of art and use of funds.

  Audio public comments:

  Daisy Legasca expressed concern regarding the City not considering other art pieces for the
  Library, including pieces which would honor first responders.

  Murali Vasudevan expressed concern with the necessity of the subject art piece at this
  time. He proposed referring this project to the City’s Fine Arts and Historical Commission
  for further consideration.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern the City was not considering other art pieces for the Library,
  including pieces which would honor first responders. He also expressed concern regarding
  lack of ongoing maintenance for the existing public art pieces.

  Sam Desai expressed concern with expending resources at this time on public art pieces.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to refer consideration of art pieces in
  the identified space at the Cerritos Library to the Fine Arts and Historical Commission and
  request they provide their recommendations to the City Council for final review and
  approval (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  (continued)

  The motion carried (4 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  Barrows
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9E.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS DENOUNCING HATE CRIMES AGAINST ASIAN
  AMERICANS OR ANY PERSON (COUNCIL).

  Mayor Solanki read a statement into the record stating the City’s opposition to hate crimes
  against Asian Americans or any person.

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Daisy Legasca spoke in support of the subject resolution and expressed opposition to hate
  crimes against any individual.

  Sam Desai spoke in support of the subject resolution and noted it was an opportunity to
  provide education about the impact of hate crimes against any individuals.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to revise the subject resolution
  as presented in the official agenda report by deleting the fifth “whereas” statement, and
  waive full reading of and adopt Resolution No. 2021-04, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS DENOUNCING HATE CRIMES AGAINST
  ASIAN AMERICANS OR ANY PERSON (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Hu, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 25, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 7

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were given by Councilmember Yokoyama and Mayor Pro Tem Vo.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to publicly post information confirming that
  Mayor Pro Tem Chuong Vo is the current Mayor Pro Tem for the City of Cerritos in order to
  correct misinformation which is circulating in the community.

12.  Closed Session

  None.

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 11:17 p.m. in memory of Marcella Kroupa McMahon.

  /s/Vida Barone
  Vida Barone, City Clerk/Agency Secretary

/s/Naresh Solanki
Naresh Solanki, Mayor/Chair
